Stated Claim / Post Context:
Strict Gun Laws Fail To Stop South African Slaughter By Gunmen With AK-47s

‘The suspects arrived and opened fire’

Actual Article Body:
(Photo by EMMANUEL CROSET / AFP via Getty Images)

At least 17 people were killed in a Saturday shooting in a Johannesburg bar despite strict gun-control laws imposed by South Africa.

The shooting, carried out by at least eight gunmen using handguns and AK-47 assault rifles, took place in the West Rand District township of Wedela, CNN reported. Despite the passage of a strict gun-control law in 2000, South Africa has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 44 homicides per 100,000 population in 2022, according to the World Bank.(RELATED:EXCLUSIVE: ‘Absolute Hate’ Farm Attack Victim Recounts Experience With Anti-White Ravagers)

“It is alleged that patrons were drinking inside and outside the tavern when the suspects arrived and opened fire on those outside. The suspects then entered the tavern and continued shooting at patrons inside,” South Africa police posted on X.

#sapsGP [GAUTENG POLICE LAUNCH MANHUNT AFTER 17 PEOPLE KILLED IN WEDELA TAVERN SHOOTING]Gauteng police have launched a manhunt for eight unidentified armed men following a deadly shooting at a tavern in Extension 3, Wedela, West Rand District, on Saturday, 26 September 2026, at… pic.twitter.com/2G4jNsYcU6

South Africa requires prospective gun owners to first obtain a “competency certificate” for the given class of firearm before they can even apply for a license to possess the gun, which costs 88 rand, or about $5.35 based on exchange rates as of Monday. The certificate cannot be applied for unless an applicant has provided proof of passing a written test and receiving firearms training, filled out an 11-page application form and even then, it can be left up to the discretion of the police.

Once the competency certificate is issued, the applicant can apply for the actual firearms license, where they pay 175 rand (roughly $10.64) to apply, fill out a 12-page form listing all firearms currently owned and the reason for purchasing a new firearm, provide fingerprints and submit to an inspection of their means for securing firearms.

States like Colorado and Washington have enacted permit-to-purchase schemes that included training requirements. The Virgin Islands engaged in litigation with the Department of Justice over its licensing law, which included a home inspection.

A second mass shooting in Cape Town claimed ten lives, CNN reported.
